what: The best action coverage each live scenario has shown over the surface it could address, and the published actions a farm fixture cannot reach.
howRead: tools/live-run/analysis/action-breadth.mjs --result <bundle>; attempted actions against the run's own published `snapshotCensus` (the families its snapshots carried a row for), joined to actions through tools/lib/stardew-published-action-registry.mjs and TARGET_FIELD
why: A count of executions cannot tell a varied day from 124 repetitions of three safe actions. `round39` reported
`executionTrace: { ok: true, rows: 124 }` and completed, having addressed a small part of the world it was
given, and nothing in its artifact said so. This file is the ratchet that makes the next such run visible: a
run below the recorded best is `narrow:below_baseline:<label>`.
THE DENOMINATOR. Coverage is `attempted / addressable`, never `attempted / 95`: a target-bound action is only
constructible while its `*Targets` family has a row in the snapshot, one `FixtureScenario` arms one world, and
the first version of this ratchet therefore charged the companion for the fixture's world. `addressable` is what
the run's own census allowed, so a different fixture scenario cannot make the ratchet lie.
WHAT IS NOT HERE. `addressable` is null on the entry below on purpose: `round38`'s bundle publishes no census,
so its addressable width is not a number this gate ever measured, and the ratchet every later run is compared
against must not rest on a figure derived outside the gate. Its attempted count (24), family count (11) and
per-family split were measured against the catalog and are kept as the ratchet's family dimension.
HOW A RUN IS COMPARED. `coverageFloor` is the best coverage a census-bearing run of this scenario has shown, with
its OWN attempted/addressable pair: a run below it did not use the surface its own world offered. The family
dimension compares coverage of the SAME families - the ones this run's world offered and `round38` also worked in -
never an absolute family count, which vetoed farm-only days for the mine trips their fixture never had. A family the
run's world never offered is not asked of it, and one it offered and skipped is named in the verdict.

coverageFloor.label: round76
coverageFloor.measured: 17 of the 43 actions its own three days made addressable (39.5%), in 9 of the 20 families, largest single action 21.2% (cut_weeds) - the first census-bearing multiday run on this machine. It is a FLOOR for the coverage dimension, not a width for `round38`: round38's own denominator predates the census, and putting its attempted count beside another run's width would be a comparison identity no run ever had.

multiday_routine.measured: 24 distinct actions in 11 families over 379 executions, largest single action 22% (break_rock) - the widest multiday day on this machine out of the 172 multiday bundles that carry an attempted list
multiday_routine.addressableNotRecorded: this bundle predates `snapshotCensus`, so the gate measures it as not_measured:no_snapshot_census and records no width for it; the coverage dimension is compared against `coverageFloor` instead, and the first census-bearing multiday run that beats the floor re-records both

exclusions.reason: elevator-floor action: the floor set is not a client-supplied range, it is what `MineElevatorMenu` displays (integrations/stardew/src/Core/Models/BridgeProtocolModels.cs:614-630), so a fixture that has never descended a mine publishes no floor to select and the current floor is a native no-op

multiplayer-only: the one social act that is not about an NPC in front of the actor, sent to the whole lobby through `Multiplayer.sendChatMessage` (integrations/stardew/src/Core/Policy/FarmhandActionDefinitions.cs:882-885); a native-local farm fixture has one farmhand and no peer to reach

needs a Raft in a tool slot (integrations/stardew/src/Core/Policy/FarmhandActionDefinitions.cs:528, `ToolResource("raft", ...)`) and open water beside it; the native-local fixture's player starts with no raft and no farm day places one

targets the Bus Stop ticket machine of the current location (integrations/stardew/src/Core/Protocol/BridgeProtocol.cs:2394-2396) and drives `BusStop.checkAction+answerDialogue` (integrations/stardew/src/Core/Policy/FarmhandActionDefinitions.cs:515-526); the bus is out of order until the Vault repair, which a fixture that starts a fresh farm has not done
